summary: Over the next ten weeks Microsoft switches on AI features and AI spending unless someone says no. Claude arrives in Swiss and EU tenants on 9 December. Metered Copilot experiences show up from January, and pay-as-you-go billing for Copilot Business follows in Q1 2027. Each setting needs a decision and an owner before its date.
tradeoff: Over the next ten weeks Microsoft switches on AI features and AI spending, unless someone switches them off first. Claude models go live for all users in Swiss and EU tenants on 9 December unless an admin opts out. From the end of January, every licensed user will see metered Cowork, Code and Autopilot. In Q1 2027, new Copilot Business orders come with usage-based billing switched on, capped at 4,000 Copilot Credits per user per month. Copilot Chat limits are already nudging unlicensed staff to request or buy seats. Saying yes to all of this speeds up adoption. It also brings in a new AI subprocessor and a bill that grows with use, and the tenant fills up with more non-human identities. Nobody actually decided any of it.

Do we let vendor defaults set the pace and check afterwards? Or do we opt out across the board and accept that blocked demand moves to shadow AI? That second risk isn't theoretical. DNSFilter reports that 20.1% of organisations have already had a security incident from an unapproved AI connection.

Decide each setting before its date, and write down who owns it. Scope Claude to specific groups by 9 December. Before the next Copilot order, set spending limits below that credit cap. Let staff request metered experiences by role, and move third-party AI apps to admin consent. Opting in is fine, as long as someone actually chose to.

pillars.name: Financial & Licensing Realities
pillars.subtitle: Seats become seats plus a meter
pillars.reality: From 1 December, Copilot can be bought without a Microsoft 365 base licence, and new SKU IDs replace the '(add-on)' offers for new purchases. The bigger change comes in Q1 2027. New Copilot Business orders through CSP then switch on pay-as-you-go, and a single new order also turns on metering for the Copilot Business licences you already have. Buy one seat, meter them all. Meanwhile, analysts estimate that about one in three paid Copilot seats goes unused in a typical week.
pillars.action: Ask your CSP when this goes live for you. Before the next Copilot Business order, set tenant spending limits and alerts below the credit cap from the trade-off above. At renewal, reclaim seats that have been idle for 28 days or more. Quote templates and software asset management rules need the new SKU IDs too, because anything that matches on the old offer names stops matching.

pillars.name: Governance & Data Hygiene
pillars.subtitle: Every AI path needs an owner
pillars.reality: Several new ways into company data open within a few weeks. On 9 December Claude becomes a Microsoft subprocessor in everyday use. Agent identities aren't covered by Conditional Access policies aimed at 'all users', so in Entra 'all' turns out to mean 'all humans'. A new built-in policy will also disable idle agents after 60 days. And employees keep granting third-party AI tools OAuth access, which 43% of organisations only find out about afterwards, or never.
pillars.action: Legal and Security should record the Anthropic choice before 9 December and update the record of processing activities. For agents, start with an inventory and give each one a human sponsor. Then add agent-targeted Conditional Access in report-only mode, so you see what it would block before it blocks anything. Third-party apps should go through the admin consent workflow in Entra.

pillars.name: Digital Employee Experience
pillars.subtitle: Patch regressions and sign-in changes hit the helpdesk
pillars.reality: Printing is back on the problem list, where it has always felt at home. The November Windows updates can fail to print documents with invisible zero-size images, such as watermarks or generated templates. They also broke KMS activation scripts until the 13 November out-of-band fix, and October's LDAP hardening can cut access to some NetApp SMB shares. Admins report NTLM signing breaking App Volumes in VDI. On the sign-in side, some SMS and voice MFA sign-ins now show a CAPTCHA, and cross-tenant calendars with partners break unless they're moved off EWS.
pillars.action: Keep the security update deployed. This week, ask the template owners in Finance, Legal and HR to test the documents they really need to print. NTLM signing becomes mandatory in May 2027, and starting the audit now is cheaper than starting it in April. The helpdesk needs scripts for the MFA CAPTCHA and the Copilot Chat limits. After 23 November, move cross-tenant calendar sharing together with the partner admins.

pillars.name: Culture, Adoption & Change Velocity
pillars.subtitle: Demand shows up in the request queue
pillars.reality: Assigned licences say little about adoption, as the idle-seat estimate in Pillar 1 shows. Meanwhile, Copilot Chat limit prompts and the new 'Request access' buttons will create a steady stream of requests from staff. Picture Adele Vance in Finance hitting the Chat limit, clicking 'Request access' and hearing nothing back. If IT blocks requests without an approved alternative, people like Adele move to unapproved tools.
pillars.action: Treat licence and access requests as your best demand signal. Send them through one approval path that asks which business process the seat will speed up. Point 'Learn more' to internal guidance with examples from your champions, and let HR own and publish an acceptable-use policy that names the approved tools. When you report on adoption, report time saved in specific processes.

calls: Agree the Anthropic setting before 9 December. Agent identities need sponsors and their own Conditional Access, and the SMS and voice MFA path needs a decision before 1 February 2027.

Set Copilot spending limits below the credit cap before the next Copilot Business order. That's the urgent one. Plan the 1 December SKU change together with the renewal seat audit, and if SMS MFA stays, budget a telephony provider.

Start with printing. Can Finance, Legal and HR still print their critical templates on the November build? Then check that the out-of-band fix is in the images and that the NTLM signing audit has started. The helpdesk will need scripts for the MFA CAPTCHA and the Copilot Chat limits.
antipattern_head: Stop letting default settings and upgrade prompts make your AI decisions.
antipattern_body: This quarter, Microsoft's defaults decide who gets Claude, who sees metered agents and when consumption billing starts. Meanwhile, Chat limit prompts push staff to ask for seats. If you buy seats whenever a prompt asks, or leave settings untouched because nobody owns them, you get shelfware and unbudgeted consumption at the same time, which is quite an achievement. Every date on the cliff list below needs an owner and a recorded choice.
cliffs: Cross-tenant calendar sharing via Cross-Tenant Access Policy fully rolled out
Standalone Copilot offers; '(add-on)' offers end of sale in CSP
Viva Engage can no longer create Teams town halls
Claude models on by default for EU and EFTA tenants
Windows Server 2016 extended support and Windows 10 Enterprise LTSC 2021 updates end
Metered Copilot experiences visible to all licensed users
Usage-based billing default-on for new Copilot Business in CSP (no day set)
Microsoft-provided SMS and voice MFA delivery retires
Final EWS shutdown in Exchange Online
Windows servers require NTLM signing by default (no day set)
Microsoft Purview Data Governance end of support

items.title: Claude models switch on by default for EU and EFTA Copilot tenants
items.sowhat: Swiss and EU tenants that never made a choice get Anthropic's Claude models for all users in Copilot and Copilot Studio, with processing moving into the EU Data Boundary. The 'Microsoft 365 apps only' option is retired and moves to All users.
items.action: Pick All users, Specific users and groups, or No users this week. The setting is under Copilot > Settings > AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors > Anthropic. Then update the record of processing activities.

items.title: Copilot Business pay-as-you-go billing becomes the CSP default
items.deadline: Jan to Mar 2027, no day set
items.sowhat: A new Copilot Business purchase through a CSP partner turns on usage-based billing, capped at 4,000 Copilot Credits per user per month. It also turns on metering for the Copilot Business licences already in the tenant.
items.action: Ask the CSP partner for your go-live date. Before the next order, set a tenant spending limit below the cap, with alerts, and agree who may raise it.

items.title: SMS and voice MFA gets CAPTCHA prompts now, and Microsoft-provided delivery retires
items.sowhat: Some SMS and voice MFA attempts now need a CAPTCHA, and users behind restrictive proxies may fail to sign in. From 1 February 2027 Microsoft stops delivering SMS and voice itself, so you'll need to contract a telephony provider (Soprano, Telesign or Infobip) or move users to passkeys or Authenticator.
items.action: Count the users still on SMS or voice and brief the helpdesk. In December, decide between migration and a provider contract.

items.title: Copilot sold without a Microsoft 365 base licence; add-on offers end of sale in CSP
items.sowhat: New SKUs at the same price replace the '(add-on)' offers for new purchases, and existing subscriptions keep renewing. Quotes, scripts and reports that match on offer names will change. This lands while analysts estimate that about one in three paid seats goes unused in a typical week.
items.action: Before renewal, reclaim seats idle for 28 days or more. Update quote templates and asset management rules for the new SKU IDs. Buy standalone seats only when there's a specific use case behind them.

items.title: Copilot Cowork, Code and Autopilot become visible to every licensed user
items.sowhat: Licensed users will see metered experiences with a 'Request access' option, even where they aren't enabled. Without a rule, IT ends up running a request queue and nobody owns the question of who may spend Copilot Credits.
items.action: Set up 'Access requests to usage-based billing experiences' by role; it's available from mid-November. From mid-December, point 'Learn more' to your internal guidance.

items.title: Unpublished Copilot Chat limits now hit users without a Copilot licence
items.sowhat: Since 2 November (up to 2,000 seats) and 9 November (larger tenants), unlicensed staff hit Chat limits that admins can't see or adjust. The notice then nudges them to request or buy a licence.
items.action: Give the helpdesk a standard answer and turn off Copilot self-service purchase. Licence requests should go through one approval path, together with Procurement.

items.title: AI agent identities get lifecycle guardrails; 'all users' Conditional Access misses agents
items.sowhat: A built-in inactivity policy (preview, all tenants) notifies owners after 60 days and then disables idle agent identities. Policies aimed at all users don't include agent user accounts, so agents can sit outside controls that leaders assume cover everyone.
items.action: Inventory the agents and give each one a human sponsor. Seasonal agents need protection from the 60-day rule. Add agent-targeted Conditional Access in report-only mode first.

items.title: One in five organisations report an incident from an unapproved AI connection
items.sowhat: In DNSFilter's survey of 400 IT and security managers (3 Nov), 20.1% had an incident from an unapproved AI connection. 43% only learn after the fact, or never, when an AI tool gets OAuth or API access, and 40.3% put their next security budget into AI governance.
items.action: Move Entra to the admin consent workflow. HR should publish an acceptable-use policy that names the approved AI tools.

items.title: November Windows updates break some printing, KMS activation and NetApp or VDI workflows
items.sowhat: Documents with invisible zero-size images may not print. KMS scripts failed until the 13 November out-of-band fix, LDAP hardening can cut NetApp SMB access, and admins report NTLM signing breaking App Volumes in VDI.
items.action: Keep the update deployed. This week, owners of invoice, contract and payslip templates should test printing. Start the NTLM signing audit with events 4022 and 4023.

items.title: Cross-tenant free/busy and calendar sharing must move off Exchange Web Services
items.sowhat: Free/busy, MailTips and calendar sharing with partner organisations break unless they're moved to Microsoft 365 Cross-Tenant Access Policy. The EWS extension only lasts until the final shutdown on 1 April 2027.
items.action: Run the affected-tenant checks and list the suppliers and subsidiaries that depend on them. Once the 23 November rollout lands, migrate together with their admins.

discarded: Release Planner retirement, the legacy Teams GitHub app, the Outlook usage report leaving the Exchange admin centre, Defender for Identity classic alert retirement, Word legacy compatibility settings, Teams mobile and Queues features, self-healing KB5132061 install loops, Partner Center sandbox renames, and January 2027 currency changes (AUD, CNY, INR, NOK and NZD only; no CHF or EUR change). Routine admin work with no strategic trade-off.
method: Signals from 2 to 16 November 2026 across Message Center, Partner Center, Entra and security advisories, admin community reporting and analyst research, kept only if they move budget, open a risk or governance gap, or create friction that needs IT, HR, Security, Procurement, Finance or Legal to align. Message Center items link to the public mirror at mc.merill.net. First Page Sage and DNSFilter figures are their own estimates and survey results.
